high.title: Dollar-Won Edges Closer to 1,520 Mark as Iran Peace Talks Falter
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate surged dramatically to 1,519.00 won, jumping 14.70 won from the previous Seoul market close and approaching the critical 1,520 level. This represents significant won weakness driven by heightened geopolitical risk aversion as doubts emerged over US-Iran peace negotiations. Despite a rally in US equities, the Korean won reflected safe-haven demand for dollars amid Middle East tensions. The sharp overnight move suggests potential BOK intervention risks if the rate breaks above 1,520. For traders, this marks a key inflection point where currency authorities may step in to defend the won. The rapid 14.70 won move overnight indicates high volatility and thin liquidity conditions that could persist until geopolitical tensions ease.

high.title: Dollar-Won Rises to 1,512.90 on Risk Aversion as Iran Considers 'Expanding Front'
high.summary: The USD/KRW broke above 1,510 won to close at 1,512.90, up 5.00 won from the previous Seoul close and 8.60 won from the day session. Risk-off sentiment dominated as Iran threatened to completely blockade the Strait of Hormuz and expand the Middle East conflict in response to Israeli attacks on Lebanon. Iran also suspended US dialogue, escalating regional tensions and driving safe-haven demand for dollars. This geopolitical premium is putting significant pressure on the Korean won, with traders watching for potential BOK intervention signals. The 8.60 won intraday surge indicates heightened volatility that could challenge Korean monetary authorities' FX stability objectives.

medium.title: [BOK Conference] BOK Board Member Lee Su-hyung - 'Monetary Policy Transmission Channels Critical in Digital Economy'
medium.summary: BOK Monetary Policy Board member Lee Su-hyung highlighted concerns that digital currencies and non-bank institutions could weaken traditional monetary policy transmission channels. He warned that stablecoins operating outside central bank scope could reduce monetary policy effectiveness if their usage expands, signaling potential regulatory scrutiny ahead.

medium.title: [BOK Conference] Kashkari - Tokenization is This Year's 'Buzzword'... Stablecoins Also Need Regulation
medium.summary: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari expressed skepticism about financial tokenization trends and argued stablecoins should face bank-level regulation. His comments at the BOK conference suggest international central bank alignment on digital currency oversight, potentially influencing Korean regulatory approaches.

medium.title: Korean Air Bond Sale Draws Strong Demand on Positive Outlook, 2-Year Notes Price Below Double-Digit Spread
medium.summary: Korean Air successfully raised 200 billion won in corporate bonds with total orders reaching 1.114 trillion won. The strong demand allowed 2-year notes to price with single-digit spreads over benchmarks, indicating healthy domestic credit markets and investor appetite for quality Korean corporate debt.

medium.title: [Market Close] KOSPI Hits 8,800 High Amid Wild Swings - 'Leveraged ETFs Amplify Volatility'
medium.summary: The KOSPI reached a record high above 8,800 but experienced heightened volatility attributed to new leveraged ETFs tracking individual stocks. Samsung Electronics gained 3.30% while market swings were amplified by the new leveraged products, suggesting structural changes in Korean equity market dynamics.
